legacy_root.question: What must a marketplace's published governance say (who may publish, how a dispute is raised, how a takedown is decided, what the appeal is) when there is exactly one owner and no committee - and which mature model degrades most gracefully to N=1?
legacy_root.answer: A single-owner marketplace must publish four operational slots plus a statutory-notice channel: (1) who may publish (authenticated holder, first-come first-served, not a naming-rights broker); (2) how a dispute is raised (one named public channel; squatting is not transferred on demand; IP goes through the legal path); (3) who decides a takedown (the named Owner, at stated discretion — not a fictional committee); (4) what the appeal is (a re-review by the same Owner at a published address, explicitly not an independent tribunal). The operator-decides model (npm administrators / Hugging Face company ToS) degrades most gracefully to N=1 because the text already names an operator rather than a staffed maintainer set. The independent recusal panel that can reverse the original decision-maker cannot be honoured at N=1 and is omitted rather than faked.
